```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(reindeer)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
```

A corpus is a directory ending in `_emuDB`. `corpus(path, create = TRUE)` makes
an empty one; `import_media()` fills it from audio files.

```{r create}
root <- tempfile("build_"); dir.create(root)
corp <- corpus(file.path(root, "pilot_emuDB"), create = TRUE)
corp
```

## Import recordings

Each file becomes a bundle named after the file, in the session you name. The
whole batch is checked before anything is written: missing files, duplicate or
unsafe names, and clashes with existing bundles stop the import with nothing
changed.

```{r import}
wavs <- list.files(file.path(demo_corpus()@basePath, "0000_ses"),
                   pattern = "wav$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)[1:3]
meta <- data.frame(bundle = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(wavs)),
                   Speaker = c("P01", "P02", "P03"),
                   Gender  = c("Female", "Male", "Female"),
                   Age     = c(8, 35, 62))
import_media(corp, wavs, session = "S1", metadata = meta)
get_metadata(corp) |> select(session, bundle, Speaker, Gender, Age)
```

Per-bundle metadata can be a data frame (as here), or one named list that
applies to every file. Whatever you give is validated and written to
`METADATA.json` files; see `vignette("metadata")`.

```{r clash}
tryCatch(import_media(corp, wavs[1], session = "S1"),
         error = function(e) cat(conditionMessage(e)))
```

## Check what you have

```{r check}
summary(corp)
```

`validate_corpus()` checks every JSON file against its schema and returns a
tidy table, so problems are easy to filter and count.

## Next steps

* Annotate: `annotate(corp)` opens the corpus in Artic (`vignette("annotating")`).
* Bring in existing annotations: `vignette("interoperability")`.
* Describe and archive the result: `vignette("archiving")`.
